links.outcome: Reading grade level of ChatGPT responses to osteosarcoma questions versus recommended patient reading level
links.effect: Baseline FKGL 10.51 (English) and 10.29 (Spanish), FRES about 51.7; above the 5th-6th grade recommended level, and still 8.27 and 7.2 after simplification.
links.quote: Thus, ChatGPT responses for osteosarcoma related queries may not be at an appropriate level for the general population emphasizing the need for physician oversight and simplification command.

links.outcome: Change in readability after asking ChatGPT to 'Make text easier to understand'
links.effect: English FRES 51.8 to 63.3 and FKGL 10.51 to 8.27; Spanish FRES 51.6 to 66.1 and FKGL 10.29 to 7.2 (all p<0.001), though simplified text remained above 5th-6th grade level.
links.quote: While the modifications significantly improved the readability within each respective language, when comparing between English and Spanish it was better at modifying English responses.

unlisted_practices: Follow-up simplification prompt to improve readability of LLM patient responses
Physician filtering and oversight of LLM patient-facing responses

links.effect: English FRES/FKGL improved to 63.3/8.27; Spanish to 66.1/7.2; paired tests for both languages p < 0.001.
links.quote: While the modifications significantly improved the readability within each respective language, when comparing between English and Spanish it was better at modifying English responses.

links.effect: No baseline difference: FRES p = 0.307, FKGL p = 0.294; after modification, language differences were significant: p = 0.003 and p = 0.011.
links.quote: There was a statistically significant difference in comprehensibility of English responses compared to Spanish responses with FRES and the FKGL after modification between both languages ( p = 0.003 and p = 0.011).

links.effect: No factually inaccurate English or Spanish responses; average accuracy Likert scores were 4.5 and 4.6.
links.quote: In both English and Spanish, none of the ChatGPT generated responses were found to be factually inaccurate.

links.outcome: reading grade level of AI-generated responses
links.effect: Baseline English responses had an average FRES of 51.8 and FKGL of 10.51 (10th grade), while Spanish responses had FRES 51.6 and FKGL 10.29, exceeding average patient literacy levels.
links.quote: The average original FRES was 51.8 making it moderately difficult to understand and the FKGL was 10.51 corresponding to a 10th grade reading level.

links.outcome: language subgroup disparity in comprehensibility improvement
links.effect: Comprehensibility differed significantly between English and Spanish responses after modification (p = 0.003 and p = 0.011), with Spanish responses showing worse comprehensibility and lower clinical sufficiency (60% vs 100%).
links.quote: Comprehension was found to be worse with Spanish responses than English.

links.effect: None of the responses in English or Spanish were factually inaccurate, with average Likert accuracy ratings of 4.5/5 in English and 4.6/5 in Spanish.
links.quote: In both English and Spanish, none of the ChatGPT generated responses were found to be factually inaccurate.

unlisted_practices: Prompting large language models with a simplification command ('Make text easier to understand') to reduce reading grade level
